title: Unique differential on one filtered-complex quotient page
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], $K^\bullet$ an integer-indexed cochain complex, and $F$ a decreasing filtration by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration]. Fix $r\in\mathbb Z$ with $r\ge1$. Write $Z_r^{p,q}=F.\mathrm{complexCycles}(p,p+q,r)$ and $B_r^{p,q}=F.\mathrm{complexBoundaries}(p,p+q,r)$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients], and form the actual object $Q_r^{p,q}=\operatorname{coker}(B_r^{p,q}\hookrightarrow Z_r^{p,q})$ using [lem-sp-filtered-complex-boundaries-le-cycles]. There is a unique family of morphisms between these quotient objects, zero outside bidegree $(r,1-r)$ [def-sp-spectral-sequence], with square zero and the following representative equation. For any object A, related bidegrees i,j, maps t:A->F^(i.1)K^(i.1+i.2) and tprime:A->F^(j.1)K^(j.1+j.2), and maps x:A->Z_r^i and y:A->Z_r^j, if dt=tprime in K and x,y project respectively to the graded classes of t,tprime, then x followed by the quotient projection and the differential equals y followed by the target quotient projection. This is exactly the data type FilteredComplexPageDifferential; no successor homology is asserted.

proof.text: Use the proved boundaries-in-cycles inclusion to construct every Q_r as a cokernel, with its cycles-to-quotient projection.

Restrict d to R = F^p K^n intersect d-inverse(F^(p+r)K^(n+1)). It lands in F^(p+r)K^(n+1) intersect ker d. Project to the target quotient. If two representatives have the same class in the graded cycles, their difference is in R intersect F^(p+1). Its differential is a target r-boundary, because the incoming filtration degree for that target is (p+r)-r+1 = p+1. Thus the map descends to graded cycles. A source boundary is represented by d of an incoming representative and has zero differential, so it also descends through the source boundary cokernel.

Set nonrelated differentials to zero. On related bidegrees, successive differentials vanish by d squared = 0. The equation on representatives holds by construction. The representative projection onto graded cycles is epic: adding F^(p+1) before the graded projection does not change its image. Compose with the epic cycles-to-Q_r projection. This composite is epic and forces uniqueness of the differential on every related pair; nonrelated pairs are zero. Proof irrelevance gives uniqueness of the full data record.
